issues.description: validate_conda uses substring match that accepts non-conda executables (e.g., 'condarc', 'mambabin', or any output containing the substring)
issues.detail: In spyder/utils/conda.py, `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'])` performs a naive substring check on stdout. Because the list order is checked unanchored, any binary whose --version output happens to contain the substring 'conda' (e.g., a wrapper, a custom script printing 'configured for conda use', or even unrelated tools) will validate. Worse, micromamba's --version output is just a version string like '1.5.6' on some builds — it may not contain the word 'micromamba' at all (micromamba prints only the version). This means a real micromamba can fail validation while unrelated executables pass.

issues.description: File filter `*.exe` makes the file picker unusable on macOS and Linux
issues.detail: In spyder/plugins/maininterpreter/confpage.py the create_browsefile call uses `filters='*.exe'`. Conda/mamba/micromamba executables on macOS and Linux have no extension. Users on non-Windows platforms will see an empty file dialog and be unable to select their conda binary. The filter must be platform-aware (e.g., '*.exe' on Windows, '*' otherwise) or simply allow all files.

issues.description: Fallback to custom conda_path only kicks in when find_conda() returns falsy — custom setting cannot override a wrong auto-detected conda
issues.detail: In kernelspec.py the new logic only consults `custom_conda`/`conda_path` if `find_conda()` returned nothing. If find_conda() picks up the wrong conda (e.g., a system conda the user explicitly wants to bypass), the user's custom selection is silently ignored. The intent stated in the confpage tooltip ('Use the specified Conda, Mamba or Micromamba instead of finding the executable from the interpreter path') is not honored — it should take precedence whenever `custom_conda` is True.

issues.description: validate_conda runs a subprocess on every keystroke / validation cycle without timeout
issues.detail: validate_conda calls run_program(...).communicate() with no timeout. If a user accidentally points the path at a hanging executable, a script that prompts for input, or a slow network-mounted binary, the preferences dialog will block indefinitely. A timeout (e.g., communicate(timeout=5)) and proper cleanup of the process on timeout is needed; alternately validation should be deferred to a save action rather than firing per edit.

issues.description: No validation that the conda_path config value is sane at the consumption site
issues.detail: kernelspec.py uses `self.get_conf('conda_path', ...)` and passes it through to `conda_version(conda_executable=conda_exe)` and downstream activation logic without re-running validate_conda. The preference page validates on entry, but the path may become stale (binary deleted, permissions changed) by the time the kernel launches. The error path then surfaces as an obscure kernel start failure rather than a clear 'configured conda executable is missing/invalid' message.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for empty string, which lets user save 'custom_conda=True' with an empty path
issues.detail: validate_conda returns True when `conda_executable == ''`. Combined with the checkbox `custom_conda`, a user can enable the checkbox, leave the path empty, save preferences, and the kernel will then fail at launch (the kernelspec fallback uses `if not conda_exe` which is True for ''). The save path should either prevent enabling `custom_conda` with an empty path, or validate_conda should reject empty when the checkbox is on.

issues.description: create_browsefile signature change is not backward-compatible for downstream callers that subclass/override
issues.detail: The new keyword arguments `validate_callback` and `validate_reason` are added to `create_browsefile` and forwarded to `create_lineedit`. The diff does not show `create_lineedit` accepting these kwargs — if `create_lineedit` does not already support them, this will raise TypeError for every existing caller. Verify that `create_lineedit` already supports validate_callback/validate_reason, otherwise this breaks all existing browsefile usages.

issues.description: setFocus() after file selection may steal focus unexpectedly
issues.detail: In `select_file`, adding `edit.setFocus()` after `edit.setText(filename)` changes existing behavior for all browsefile widgets in Spyder, not just this new one. This is a global side effect introduced by a feature-scoped PR and could affect other preference pages or dialogs. Consider scoping the focus change or documenting the rationale.

issues.description: Substring match order in validate_conda is fragile but works coincidentally
issues.detail: The check `for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda']` happens to be ordered most-specific-first, but since it's `in` substring matching (not equality) and the result is OR'd via `any()`, the ordering does not actually matter — but the comment/intent suggests the author may have believed it did. A cleaner implementation would parse the first token of `--version` output and compare exactly.

issues.description:
Error message uses HTML (

, ) but SpyderKernelError may render it as plain text in some surfaces
issues.detail:
The updated error message in kernelspec.py embeds HTML tags. If any consumer of SpyderKernelError displays the message in a context that doesn't interpret HTML (logs, stderr, plain QLabel without rich text), users will see literal `

` and `` tokens. Verify all rendering paths or use a format-agnostic message.

issues.description: Hardcoded styleSheet 'margin-left: 3px' couples to current theme/HiDPI assumptions
issues.detail: `conda_path.setStyleSheet('margin-left: 3px')` hardcodes a pixel offset. This won't scale on HiDPI displays and may conflict with theme stylesheets. Prefer layout-based indentation (a QHBoxLayout with stretch/spacer) or use Spyder's theming helpers if available.

issues.description: No migration / handling for existing users who already hit the old error and may now have stale state
issues.detail: The config default `conda_path: ''` and `custom_conda: False` are safe for new installs, but no UX is provided to surface 'hey, you previously hit the conda-not-found error; here's the new fix.' The improved error message points users to the new preference, which mitigates this, but a one-time notification or test on upgrade would be a nicer touch.

dissents.topic: Whether custom conda_path should override find_conda() unconditionally

positions.position: When `custom_conda` is checked, the user explicitly asked to use their executable. find_conda()'s result must be ignored in that case — otherwise the option is misleading.
Current behavior (auto-detect first, fall back to custom) is safer: users who toggle the checkbox by accident still get a working kernel. The UI copy could be updated to match.
On macOS/Linux this makes the file picker effectively unusable — the feature ships broken on two of three supported platforms.
Users can typically still type the path manually or change the filter dropdown in the dialog; not strictly a merge blocker, just sloppy.

dissents.topic: Whether validate_conda's substring check is adequate

positions.position: It's a preference-time sanity check, not a security boundary. Loose matching is fine and avoids false negatives across micromamba's varied output formats.
Substring matching on stdout invites false positives and obscures the actual contract (the tool must be conda/mamba/micromamba). Parse the first token or check `--help` output.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful escape hatch for users whose conda/mamba installs aren't auto-detected, and the overall shape (config key, preference UI, validator, fallback at kernel launch) is sound. However, two issues likely block merge: the `*.exe` file filter breaks the picker on macOS/Linux, and `validate_conda`'s substring-on-stdout check is both too loose (false positives) and potentially too strict (micromamba's `--version` often prints only a version number, no tool name). Additional concerns: the custom conda path is only consulted when auto-detect fails (contradicting the UI copy), the validator has no subprocess timeout, and the path isn't re-checked at kernel launch. A small set of corrections — platform-aware filter, robust validator with timeout, override-semantics fix, and verifying `create_lineedit` accepts the new kwargs — would make this ready.
